newsitem.title: NORWAY: Swedish ship to leave Norway port with stowaways.
newsitem.headline: Swedish ship to leave Norway port with stowaways.

text.p: A Swedish cargo ship stuck at a Norwegian port for three days with stowaways on board prepared to leave for Sweden on Wednesday, the national news agency NTB said.

Bengt Skold, captain of the vessel Nordoen, agreed to leave Karmoey port near Stavanger in southwestern Norway after Norwegian authorities said five policemen would guarantee the safety of the crew on the trip, NTB said.
"I feel good about raising anchor now that we are getting Norwegian police protection," he was quoted as saying.

Skold, who expected to leave for the Swedish port of Gothenburg late on Wednesday, had said the eight North African stowaways, some of whom had started a hunger strike, would pose too great a risk at sea.
Swedish maritime authorities agreed to let the ship sail to Gothenburg, where it would arrive on Friday, he said.

Norway turned down an appeal for asylum from the stowaways late on Tuesday and refused to let them ashore. Officials said the stowaways did not come from Algeria, which they claimed, but from Morocco and thus did not qualify for asylum.

One stowaway was quoted by NTB as sayingthey sneaked on board the cargo ship earlier this month in a Moroccan port. Discovered about 10 days ago by crew members, the stowaways were kept in two cabins.
